### Follow-up Questions
- What oven temperature and pan setup give the best browning for each vegetable family (roots, brassicas, alliums, squash), and when does a mixed tray need staggered start times?
- How do oil choice and amount affect caramelization and crispness, compared with dry-roasting or parboiling first?
- Which acid-herb-seed combinations suit each season (e.g., spring asparagus with lemon, dill and sunflower seeds; autumn squash with sherry vinegar, sage and pepitas)?
- Can roasted vegetables be batch-prepped for the week without losing texture, and which ones reheat best?
- What chemistry separates browning from burning (Maillard reaction vs. caramelization), and how does moisture or crowding the pan slow it down?

### Related Materials
- **Serious Eats: "The Food Lab's Guide to Roasting Vegetables"** (J. Kenji López-Alt): tests temperatures, cuts and pan crowding. https://www.seriouseats.com/the-food-lab
- **Salt Fat Acid Heat, "Acid" chapter and companion site** (Samin Nosrat): why a final squeeze of lemon makes roasted food taste brighter. https://www.saltfatacidheat.com
- **NYT Cooking: "How to Roast Vegetables"** guide: a reference for times and temperatures by vegetable. https://cooking.nytimes.com/guides
- **Bon Appétit Basically: roasted vegetable formulas**: approachable templates for finishing with herbs, seeds and dressings. https://www.bonappetit.com/basically
- **America's Test Kitchen: "Preheating the Sheet Pan" technique**: puts the vegetables on a hot pan so the cut sides sear right away. https://www.americastestkitchen.com
- **Harold McGee on the Maillard reaction** (essays and *On Food and Cooking* excerpts): the science behind browning flavour. https://www.curiouscook.com
- **Seasonal Food Guide**: a tool that shows which vegetables are in season by US state and month. https://www.seasonalfoodguide.org

### Book & Podcast Recommendations
**Books**
- ***Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat*** by Samin Nosrat: its framework explains why the lemon finish in this note works and how to adjust it.
- ***Plenty More*** by Yotam Ottolenghi: it has a whole chapter on roasted vegetables, many finished with citrus, herbs and seeds.
- ***The Food Lab*** by J. Kenji López-Alt: it tests the roasting variables (heat, fat, surface area) through experiments.

**Podcasts**
- ***The Splendid Table***, hosted by Francis Lam: episodes on seasonal vegetable cooking give practical ideas for finishing roasted vegetables.
- ***Home Cooking*** with Samin Nosrat and Hrishikesh Hirway: listener questions about vegetables often turn into acid-and-herb finishing tips.
- ***Gastropod***, hosted by Cynthia Graber and Nicola Twilley: its science-and-history episodes on flavour and browning give the technique context.
